- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast by 5–10% for recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices during strong negative sentiment (sentiment < -1.0) — add 5–10% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days) — apply a 1–2 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% on next day.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid overconfidence in early forecast days — dampen first 5–7 days by 3–5% if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- If sentiment turns sharply negative after forecast, apply a “safety margin” — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
